mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'X has more than Y' (including 'X has N more than Y') as a signed difference X − Y = N, preserving the order presented.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes one person having more (or fewer) items than another, possibly with a numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Treating 'Alice has more than Bob' as an absolute difference or ignoring the sign, leading to an incorrect equation.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer 'X gives N to Y' occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating each person's count accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem includes a statement that one person gives a number of items to another.
mathgap.example: Adding N to both X and Y, or subtracting from Y instead of X, resulting in wrong counts.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a distinct variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation, building a complete system of constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After extracting all relevant statements, before attempting to solve for unknowns.
mathgap.example: Failing to create a variable for a person mentioned only in a transfer, causing an incomplete system.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order as presented.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement refers to the difference between two persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between X and Y' as an absolute value, losing sign information.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements first, updating each person's count, and then use those updated counts when interpreting relational equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing transfer statements and before handling any difference or 'has more than' equations.
mathgap.example: Using a person's pre‑transfer count in a later difference equation, leading to an incorrect relationship.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat statements that give an explicit count (e.g., 'X has N items') as the initial amount before any transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct count statement in the problem description.
mathgap.example: Assuming the given count is the final count after transfers, causing mismatched totals.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: 'The final answer is \boxed{<integer>}'
mathgap.when_to_apply: After computing the answer, before returning the response.
mathgap.example: Omitting the LaTeX box or using a different phrasing, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

mathgap.title: Aggregate multiple transfers per person
mathgap.principle: Sum all incoming and outgoing transfer amounts for each person to obtain a net change, then apply that net change to the person's count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person is involved in more than one transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Applying each transfer sequentially without aggregating, leading to double‑counting or missed updates.

mathgap.title: Complete system solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all constraints into linear equations, actually solve the system (or directly isolate the target variable) to obtain the numeric answer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Once the full set of equations is assembled, before outputting the answer.
mathgap.example: Leaving the system unsolved and guessing a value, resulting in an incorrect answer.

mathgap.title: Filter relevant statements
mathgap.principle: When parsing the problem, only translate statements that involve the target object (e.g., grapes, raspberries) into constraints; ignore statements about ages, personalities, marriage years, etc., as they do not affect the counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: During the initial extraction phase, before building equations.
mathgap.example: Including a person's age as a numeric constraint on their raspberry count, leading to an inconsistent system.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes that the given explicit counts already include any later transfers, ignoring the order of events.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret explicit count statements as initial amounts before any transfers, and apply transfers afterwards.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misreads 'X gives N to Y' and adds N to X or subtracts from Y.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a transfer is described, subtract N from the giver and add N to the receiver.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats 'difference between X and Y' as |X − Y|, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret difference statements as signed differences preserving the order presented.

mathgap.description: Applying relational equations before applying transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model uses pre‑transfer counts in equations that should reflect post‑transfer values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First apply all transfers to update counts, then translate relational statements.

mathgap.description: Incomplete solving: failing to derive the answer from the constraints, leading to a guess
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model stops before solving the full system, often due to complexity or oversight.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Ensure all extracted constraints are assembled into a solvable system and solve for the target variable before answering.
